#### Business rules extracted
- **BR-PG2-199** — Managed Space Operators are restricted to posting only Managed Space listings. _(§ Business Rules 1)_
- **BR-PG2-200** — If a Managed Space Tenant opts for Managed Space, the posted requirement is visible only to the Keydemand team and admin; it is hidden from external agents and operators. _(§ Business Rules 1, 2)_
- **BR-PG2-201** — Managed Office supply (property) is added ONLY by the Keydemand team and cannot be added by agents. _(§ Business Rules 1)_
- **BR-PG2-202** — Managed office operators are treated like "Developers": they cannot log in directly; Keydemand teams collect center/hub details offline and upload them manually. _(§ Business Rules 1)_
- **BR-PG2-203** — The official company or brand name must be clearly displayed whenever a demand is posted. _(§ Business Rules 1)_
- **BR-PG2-204** — "Managed Space" is a new asset class nested under "Projects", not standard property inventory; all operator inventory (individual centers or coworking hubs) is classified under "Projects". _(§ Business Rules 1, 2, 3)_
- **BR-PG2-205** — Transaction options for Managed Space projects are restricted to "Lease"; "Sale" and "Lead" parameters are removed for this asset class. _(§ Business Rules 1, 3)_
- **BR-PG2-206** — Selecting "Managed Space" as user type at registration requires: Mobile number and OTP, Name, Company name, City, Location, Number of seats. _(§ Business Rules 1)_
- **BR-PG2-207** — Managed Space Tenants can add only 1 demand at registration and are blocked from adding more unless onboarded as enterprise users. _(§ Business Rules 1)_
- **BR-PG2-208** — Registration requires mandatory T&C acceptance and offers an "Enquire for Enterprise Solution" option. _(§ Business Rules 1)_
- **BR-PG2-209** — If a profile brand image is uploaded it shows on the demand card; otherwise a placeholder is auto-selected by asset class. _(§ Business Rules 1)_
- **BR-PG2-210** — Managed Space Tenants may explore both Managed Space and standard Office properties. _(§ Business Rules 2)_
- **BR-PG2-211** — Header items: Keydemand Logo (→ homepage), Explore Properties (properties uploaded by anyone, only the Managed Space Tenant asset class), Post Demand (only properties of Managed Space Tenant), Notifications, Enterprise Solution, Hamburger (Profile Menu), Live Dashboard. _(§ Business Rules 2; Header)_
- **BR-PG2-212** — Social-media-acquired users (LinkedIn or Meta) are redirected after registration to a city-specific Microsite showing managed supply summary, office/managed space city-specific relevancy, and an option to explore other properties. _(§ Business Rules 2)_
- **BR-PG2-213** — Matched property cards display directly below the demand; "Explore Properties" shows similar properties in the same geographical area as the active demand. _(§ Business Rules 2)_
- **BR-PG2-214** — On the Microsite, property cards are blurred with a CTA to request photos from the listing Agent. _(§ Business Rules 2)_
- **BR-PG2-215** — A request above a custom city-specific size threshold (e.g., [XYZ sq ft] in a selected city) is automatically flagged and the lead transferred to the Keydemand team for customized, offline handling. _(§ Business Rules 3)_
- **BR-PG2-216** — Managed office accounts get access features similar to an Enterprise user. _(§ Business Rules 3)_
- **BR-PG2-217** — On new registration or demand capture, an entry is logged in the admin central log and an automated WhatsApp alert is sent to the Keydemand regional representative. _(§ Business Rules 3)_
- **BR-PG2-218** — Clicking the view-contact CTA shares the contact number with the Managed Space Tenant via WhatsApp and simultaneously notifies the supplier, which is the internal Keydemand team. _(§ Business Rules 4)_
- **BR-PG2-219** — Viewing a phone number is passive (no approval); both parties instantly gain each other's contact details. _(§ Business Rules 4; Body 2.3)_
- **BR-PG2-220** — The lister receives a WhatsApp notification with Viewer's Name, User Type, Mobile Number and the Property/Demand ID viewed; the lead shows "Unread" until clicked. _(§ Business Rules 4; Body 2.3)_
- **BR-PG2-221** — The live, impromptu dashboard is built on or linked from the Homepage. _(§ Business Rules 5)_
- **BR-PG2-222** — Slider interactions: Active Demand Card → scroll to demands section; Relevancy → scroll to My Demands; Leads Received → slider with all leads, per-demand lead count opens 1 tab (Phone number viewed); Enquiries Card → 3 tabs (Projects Enquired, Numbers Viewed, Images Requested); Your Listing - Demands → full demand list. _(§ Business Rules 5; Body 2.6)_
- **BR-PG2-223** — Own demands across all asset classes are listed newest first; demands with active relevancies are prioritized first with a red dot; clicking the relevancy count shows latest matches on top marked "latest" with red dot. _(§ Business Rules 5; Body 2.1–2.2)_
- **BR-PG2-224** — Deactivate account button under profile requires confirmation via popup dialogue; deactivation pauses all activity, hides all active listings, pauses platform presence, and pauses/deactivates inventory; reactivate any time via "Reactivate account" on the homepage. _(§ Business Rules 5; Hamburger 2)_
- **BR-PG2-225** — Deletion is requested via a designated Form; the Keydemand team manually reaches out to finalize; deletion permanently deletes associated inventory. _(§ Business Rules 5; Hamburger 2)_
- **BR-PG2-226** — Post demand input fields are columns EL to EQ of Demand Input Fields; Notifications per Notifications Tab rows 136 to 156. _(§ Header 3–4)_
- **BR-PG2-227** — Hamburger: Dashboard (Overview, Demands, Leads [phone numbers viewed], Enquiries [Projects enquired, Numbers you have viewed, Images Requested]); My Demands filters Search PropertyId/title/location, Asset Class, City, Status Active/Deactivated, Sort Newest first/most leads/recent matches; Edit profile (EPIC 2, US-006; G to J in User Profile Tab); Saved Properties/Projects; Alerts & Notifications (All/Unread, WhatsApp toggle, promotional-only opt-out, WhatsApp-to-self with PDF on new demand); Help contact@keydemand.in; FAQ; Logout. _(§ Hamburger)_
- **BR-PG2-228** — Phone number viewed (leads) records Name, Mobile Number, Demand id, User-Type-I am a (F&B/Retail/Agent/Tenant//Keydemand team), Timestamp, Card (Property Id, Asset Class, Name of property, City, Location, Quoted Price, CTA- Call). _(§ Body 2.3)_
- **BR-PG2-229** — Project Interested recalls prior interest on the CTA ("You have already shown interest on <date>") and lists Name of project, Project Id, Posted by, Location, City, Possession, Listed on, View Listing. _(§ Body 2.4)_
- **BR-PG2-230** — Numbers viewed covers Keydemand team and brand/office tenant listings (Body slider: "numbers viewed of keydemand team and tenant"). _(§ Body 2.4, 2.6)_
- **BR-PG2-231** — Image requests table: Project/Property Id (clickable/redirectable), Asset Class, City, Location, Transaction Type, Posted By, Date Requested; statuses Accepted ("View Images"), Pending, Rejected ("View Listing without Images"). _(§ Body 2.4)_
- **BR-PG2-232** — Show Interest on Premium, Exclusive and Projects in \<city\> uses a profile pre-filled form (Name, Mobile, Email, User Type) and shows "Thank you for showing interest". _(§ Body 3, 4, 6)_
- **BR-PG2-233** — Reused landing sections (CTAs change when logged in): banner auto-carousel 5s; Explore Property search (City mandatory etc.); Recent Searches; New Properties; Explore properties in \<city\> "View Phone Number"; Top cluster hidden for now; popular cities "Explore"; About Keydemand videos with Request a Callback (only mobile mandatory); Footer same as landing page. _(§ Body)_

- "Transaction ... 'Sale' and 'Lead' parameters completely removed" — "Lead" likely means "Lease"? (it says only Lease remains); wording unclear.

- Supplier for contact reveal is "the internal Keydemand team" — but Microsite blurred cards request photos "from the listing Agent".
- Business Rules 5 slider: Numbers Viewed "of agent, keydemand team and tenant"; Body 2.6: "of keydemand team and tenant" (agent removed). Body 2.4 also drops "agent". Hamburger Leads still mentions agents.

### Group-level notes
#### Version history
- Each persona has two docs: an untitled-version draft (created 2026-05-31/06-01, modified 2026-06-19 to 2026-08-05) and a "Version 1.0 ..." doc (created 2026-08-09, modified 2026-09-28 / 2026-10-03). Per the authority rule, the "Version 1.0" title is the highest version, so it is AUTHORITATIVE; the untitled drafts are HISTORY. Modified dates agree (Version 1.0 docs are all newer).

#### Conflicts across docs in this group
- Office Tenant contact-view limit: Version 1.0 says max 5 (6th blocked); old Office doc says prompt after 3. Authoritative: 5.
- Managed Space demand limit: Version 1.0 says 1 demand, blocked until enterprise; old MS doc says additional demands can be added via dashboard. Authoritative: 1.
- Managed Space contact supplier: Version 1.0 says always the internal Keydemand team; old says agent or Keydemand team depending on size. Authoritative: Keydemand team.
- Brand explore scope: Version 1.0 Retail/F&B allow exploring Retail, F&B and Office; old drafts said only own asset class. Authoritative: all three.
- Office explore scope: Version 1.0 "Office and Managed Space"; old "only Tenant asset class". MS Version 1.0 is internally inconsistent (Header "only Managed Space Tenant asset class" vs Business Rules "both Managed Space and standard Office").
- Brands' free demands = 3 (Retail, F&B) vs Office/Managed Space = 1 — intentional persona difference, not a conflict.
- Chatbot: F&B Version 1.0 marks it "(Phase 2)"; Retail/Office Version 1.0 Business Rules list a self-help chatbot without phase tag; Office/MS Hamburger FAQ blank.
- Logout: present in Retail, Office, MS Version 1.0; missing in F&B Version 1.0.
- "Top cluster in <city>": "Hidden for Now - Phase 2" (Office) vs "Hidden for Now" (others).
- Demand Input Fields columns: Retail BP–BW & DA–DG; F&B none in Version 1.0 (old BZ–CP); Office DJ–DY; MS EL–EQ. Notifications rows: Retail 53–75; Office & MS 136–156; F&B none.
- Edit profile columns: Retail/F&B "M to P"; Office/MS "G to J" (User Profile tab).
- "Projects in <city>" Show Interest form: Retail lists an extra "Message" field; F&B/Office/MS do not.
- Accept/Reject on contact requests: Brands only (Retail/F&B, 2-tab Leads slider); Office/MS have no contact requests (1-tab Leads slider) — consistent with "not to Office" rule.

#### Common vs persona-specific
**Shared by all four personas (Version 1.0):**
- Live, impromptu dashboard linked from homepage; Overview/Demands/Leads/Enquiries; own demands newest first, relevancy matches pushed to top with red dot; red dot on new relevancy counter showing latest on top.
- My Demands filters (Search PropertyId/title/location, Asset Class, City, Status Active/Deactivated) and sort (Newest first, most leads, recent matches).
- Slider interactions: Active Demand Card / Relevancy scroll; Enquiries Card with 3 tabs (Projects Enquired, Numbers Viewed, Images Requested); Your Listing - Demands slider.
- Two-way contact reveal on viewing a number: number shared via WhatsApp, lister notified (in-app + WhatsApp for brands; WhatsApp for tenants) with name, user type, mobile, listing; lead "Unread" until opened.
- Outbound image request table (Project/Property Id clickable, Asset Class, City, Location, Transaction Type, Posted By, Date Requested) with Accepted/View Images, Pending, Rejected/View Listing without Images.

**Source:** Google Doc · ID `1IZWe79BBcaBqgGX4qD6znl04o3hEQrn8DymvikBkAGo` · owner pradeepa.pv@futuristglobal.com · created 2026-09-28 · modified 2026-10-06 · sections read: Business Rules (1–9), Header, Hamburger (Profile) 1–6, Body (Dashboard 1.1–1.6 + landing-page sections 3–10) · comments: none returned · read coverage: 100%

#### Content

###### Business Rules

**1. Account Management & User Permissions**
- **Onboarding & Authentication:** Keydemand team members are onboarded exclusively via the backend and log in using their mobile number and an OTP.
- **Role-Based Access:** Account creation is strictly permission-based; specific privileges are managed via the admin portal.
- **Profile Management Restrictions:** The Keydemand team cannot edit, delete, or deactivate any user profiles via the front end; all profile management must be handled at the backend.
- **Inventory Lifecycle:** Deactivation and Deletion of Keydemand team: The listings needs to be assigned to another KD team user before they delete the account or deactivate account.
- **Team Inventory Capabilities:** Keydemand members can view the inventory of other team members within their "Listings" dashboard, but they are strictly restricted to editing only their own self-listings.
- **Backup Coordination:** If multiple users are assigned to the same project, they function as backups and must coordinate their efforts offline.
- **"My Listings" CRUD Privileges:** Keydemand team must be granted full Create, Read, Update, and Delete (CRUD) privileges strictly over the properties and demands they have personally posted.
- **"Keydemand Listings" (Colleague Data):** Properties and Demands posted by other Key Demand team members must be strictly "Read-Only" for colleagues; users cannot edit, delete, or deactivate other colleague's listings.
- **Future Phase (Scope):** In a future release phase, Keydemand users will be permitted to add projects and developers directly.
- **Property and Demand Posting:** They can add Office, Retail, and F&B and managed space properties and demands.

**2. Login Flow & Dashboard Navigation**
- **Immediate Dashboard Redirect:** Keydemand users must be redirected straight to their Dashboard immediately upon logging in.
- **Mobile UX Optimization:** The mobile app interface must abandon horizontal tables in favour of a card/thumbnail-based layout to optimise screen space and usability.
- **Dashboard Routing Logic:**
  - Clicking on any user card must route the Keydemand user directly to a read-only view of that specific user's dashboard statistics.
- **Interactive Drill-Downs:** All aggregate metrics on the Dashboard (e.g., Active Properties, Active Demands, Projects) must be clickable, leading to a granular, filtered list view of the items being counted.
- **Hamburger Menu & Holistic View:** Keydemand Relationship Managers (RMs) must have a single holistic view from their user dashboard. By clicking the hamburger menu, they should see a summary of all assigned brands/tenants (demands, relevancies, contact requests, project inquiries) without needing to switch accounts.
- **Custom Side-Menu Segmentation:** A custom side-menu for keydemand users must bypass standard filters and segment views into "My" (User-specific/Assigned) vs. "Overall" (Company-wide/All). It must explicitly list: Dashboard, Profile, Listings (My/KD), Projects (Assigned/All), Enterprise Accounts (Assigned/All), High Ticket Leads (My City/Overall), Notifications, leads, and Saved/Shortlisted items.
- **Grid Toggles:** Dashboards must feature a dedicated switch to toggle between "High-Value" and "Standard" inventory views.
- **Filters & Sorting:** The dashboard must include comprehensive filtering (e.g., City) and sorting options (e.g., "Most Demands," "Most Properties Posted," "Most Leads Received").

**3. High-Ticket Lead (HTL) Ecosystem**
- **HVL Definition & Dynamic Thresholds:** Requirements exceeding specific size thresholds (e.g., >10,000 sq ft in Bangalore/Hyderabad; >5,000 sq ft in Mumbai) are classified as HTLs. The Admin must have controls in the panel to define and edit these square footage limits on a per-city basis. High-value leads are exclusively new, fresh inquiries or registrations that meet or exceed specific size (sq. ft.) thresholds based on asset class and city.
- **Cross-Asset Application:** HTL rules and automated routing based on thresholds apply across Office, Retail, and F&B asset classes.
  - Exclusion: Day-to-day operational requirements posted by existing, onboarded enterprise brands (e.g., Raymond, H&M) are not categorized as high-value leads in this context.
  - Standard Leads: If a new inquiry falls below the high-value threshold (e.g., a 6,000 sq. ft. restaurant requirement where the benchmark is 8,000), it bypasses explicit RM notification and is instantly unlocked/visible to all existing agents on the platform.
- **Tier 1 vs. Tier 2 Routing:** HTL restrictions only apply to Tier 1 markets (Bangalore, Hyderabad, Chennai, Coimbatore, Pune, Mumbai, Gurgaon, Delhi). Leads in Tier 2 cities (e.g., Jaipur, Indore) bypass this and remain open to all agents regardless of size.
- **Exclusive Routing:** HTLs are routed exclusively to the Keydemand internal roster and are completely hidden from external agents.
- **Global Access vs. Local Alerts:** While notifications for a new HTL are localized to the assigned city members, all Keydemand team members possess global access to view HTLs pan-India.
- **Manual Unlock Valve:** If the Keydemand team cannot service an HTL within a specific timeframe (e.g., 3-4 days), Admins can manually "unlock" the requirement. This pushes it into the public relevancy pool, making it visible to external agents strictly under the relevancy matching engine.
- **Agent-Added Exemption:** Demands posted directly by agents bypass HTL restrictions entirely and remain visible to other agents via relevancy matching.

**4. Visibility, Relevancy & Image Security**
- **"Posted By" Transparency:** To external audiences, internal demands/properties display as "Keydemand." However, internally, the team will see the specific name of the uploading team member (e.g., "Posted by Himanshu").
- **Exclusive Indicators:** If a demand is managed exclusively by Keydemand, the "Self-View" and explore demand screens must explicitly indicate "Keydemand Team".
- **Hidden Image Protocols:** If a listing owner selects "Do not show images", external users cannot view them. However, Keydemand teams *can* always see these images, overlaid with a banner reading "Hidden to others".
- **Thumbnail Rule:** The system must display property thumbnails to the Keydemand team in all list views, even if the primary images are hidden from public or external view.
- **Image Request CTA Prevention:** To prevent sourcing conflicts, the "View Image Request" CTA button must be completely removed (or greyed out/disabled) for Keydemand users when they view external agent properties.
- **Relevancy Matching Scope:** Keydemand team properties and demands get matched with their own postings, other KD members, agents, brands and tenants.
- **Demand Exploration Exclusivity:** The Keydemand team is the *only* party authorised to explore demands. Specifically, "Managed Space" demands are visible exclusively to Keydemand and hidden from everyone else.

**5. Enterprise Accounts Breakdown & Pipeline Management**
- **Enterprise Account Dashboard Breakdown:** The dashboard must calculate the total aggregate of enterprise users (e.g., 500) and segment them into:
  - **Assigned to Me:** Total count assigned to the logged-in user.
  - **Assigned to Others:** Balance managed by the rest of the team.
  - **Sub-Category Itemisation:** The "Assigned to Me" count must explicitly break down into itemised values for *Retail and Office Brands*, *Office Tenants*, and *Managed Spaces*.
- **Posting Restrictions:** Keydemand users assigned to a brand cannot manually post or edit demands on that brand's behalf. Enterprise requirements must be managed via bulk or single upload centrally through the Admin panel.
- **CRM Pipeline (Lite):** The Admin Dashboard tracks enterprise leads through explicit CRM stages: *New, In Discussion, Site Visit, Negotiation, Closed, Lost*. It also logs the assigned representative and the last activity date. (Phase 2)
- **Lead Statusing:** Leads for Enterprise Clients are strictly categorised as *Approved, Rejected,* or *Open*. [source has a stray "6" after this sentence]
- **Alerting & Highlights:** New relevancies, leads, and enquiries for assigned Enterprise clients must be visually highlighted with direct routing to the respective page.

**6. Action Tracking & Accountability Audits**
- **Metric Definition ("User Contacted"):** The "User Contacted" metric must increment *exclusively* when the "View Phone Number" button is clicked, as offline physical calls cannot be tracked.
- **Direct Contact CTAs:** The Keydemand team does not need to use "Request Phone Number" workflows for relevant demands; they are provided with an explicit "View Phone Number" CTA for direct, instant access.
- **Outbound Contact Logs:** "Properties Contacted" logs for Enterprise clients must capture the Property ID, associated photo, and the exact date of contact for audit purposes.
- **Lead Access Audit Trail:** Clicking the "View Requirement" CTA unlocks the lead's mobile number and automatically updates the "Viewed" status (Yes/No) with a timestamp.
- **Accountability Tracking:** A "Viewed by" column must maintain a timestamped log of exactly which Keydemand team member accessed a lead.

**7. Broker Management & Projects**
- **Broker Monitoring View:** A specialized, restricted dashboard view must exist for Business Development members to monitor the platform activity of external brokers they have onboarded. This tracks requirements added, relevancies, contact attempts, leads received, missed calls, and ignored image requests to counter broker complaints.
- **Project Addition:** Projects can only be added strictly via the backend control panel by the Admin team.
- **Project Categorization:** Projects must be sorted by "Category" (*Standard, Premium, Exclusive*) within the tables.
- **Exclusive Project Follow-up:** The Keydemand team is exclusively responsible for handling all follow-ups and contact for mandated "Exclusive" projects.
- **Enquiry Granularity:** All project lists must support a drill-down for "Enquiries Received," capturing user metadata (type, name, mobile, email, timestamp, and specific projects of interest).

**8. RM (Relationship Manager) Assignment & Lead Visibility**
- **Account-Level Assignment:** An RM is assigned at the overarching entity/account level for a specific city. For example, one RM managing Aditya Birla in Hyderabad automatically handles all its sub-brands (Peter England, Louis Philippe, etc.) for that region.
- **Nomenclature:** "RM" is strictly an internal administrative term. The end-client/brand does not need to see this specific internal title; to them, this person is simply their point of contact.
- **Cross-Collaboration ("Others" Tab):** While leads are assigned to specific RMs (visible in their "Assigned" tab), other team members can view these leads under the "Others" or "All" tabs. This allows other team members to step in and fulfill the requirement using their macro-level connections if the assigned RM fails to source an option.
- **Notifications:** Once an admin unlocks a high-value lead to all agents, notifications are only sent to agents who have a *relevant property* matching the demand, following standard regular demand workflows.

**9. Notifications & Routing**
- **Notification Filtering:** Notifications must be segmentable, allowing users to filter by specific triggers such as "All leads for my listings," "Tagged projects," or "Relevancies".
- **Enquiry Routing Logic:** The system must automate routing based on the specific interaction type (e.g., direct developer enquiries, enterprise conversion prompts, or support requests)

#### Business rules extracted
- **BR-KDT-001** — Keydemand team members are onboarded exclusively via the backend. _(§ BR 1 Onboarding & Authentication)_
- **BR-KDT-002** — Keydemand team members log in using their mobile number and an OTP. _(§ BR 1 Onboarding & Authentication)_
- **BR-KDT-003** — Account creation is strictly permission-based; specific privileges are managed via the admin portal. _(§ BR 1 Role-Based Access)_
- **BR-KDT-004** — The Keydemand team cannot edit, delete, or deactivate any user profiles via the front end; all profile management must be handled at the backend. _(§ BR 1 Profile Management Restrictions; Hamburger 2 Edit profile)_
- **BR-KDT-005** — Edit profile shows no Edit, Delete, or Deactivate buttons; these can only be done on Backend. _(§ Hamburger 2)_
- **BR-KDT-006** — Before a KD team user's account is deleted or deactivated, their listings need to be assigned to another KD team user. _(§ BR 1 Inventory Lifecycle)_
- **BR-KDT-007** — Keydemand members can view the inventory of other team members within their "Listings" dashboard but can edit only their own self-listings. _(§ BR 1 Team Inventory Capabilities)_
- **BR-KDT-008** — If multiple users are assigned to the same project, they function as backups and must coordinate their efforts offline. _(§ BR 1 Backup Coordination)_
- **BR-KDT-009** — Keydemand team have full CRUD privileges strictly over the properties and demands they have personally posted. _(§ BR 1 "My Listings" CRUD)_
- **BR-KDT-010** — Properties and Demands posted by other KD team members are strictly Read-Only; users cannot edit, delete, or deactivate colleagues' listings. _(§ BR 1 "Keydemand Listings")_
- **BR-KDT-011** — Adding projects and developers directly by Keydemand users is future-phase scope (not current). _(§ BR 1 Future Phase)_
- **BR-KDT-012** — Keydemand team can post Office, Retail, F&B and Managed space properties and demands. _(§ BR 1 Property and Demand Posting; Header 2–3)_
- **BR-KDT-013** — Keydemand users are redirected straight to their Dashboard immediately upon login. _(§ BR 2; Body intro)_
- **BR-KDT-014** — Only clicking the Keydemand logo takes the KD user back to the landing page / Home page. _(§ Body intro; Header 1)_
- **BR-KDT-015** — Mobile app must use a card/thumbnail-based layout instead of horizontal tables. _(§ BR 2 Mobile UX Optimization)_
- **BR-KDT-016** — Clicking any user card routes the KD user to a read-only view of that user's dashboard statistics. _(§ BR 2 Dashboard Routing Logic)_
- **BR-KDT-017** — All aggregate dashboard metrics (e.g., Active Properties, Active Demands, Projects) must be clickable, leading to a filtered list view of the counted items. _(§ BR 2 Interactive Drill-Downs)_
- **BR-KDT-018** — From the hamburger menu, RMs see a summary of all assigned brands/tenants (demands, relevancies, contact requests, project inquiries) without switching accounts. _(§ BR 2 Hamburger Menu & Holistic View)_
- **BR-KDT-019** — The KD side-menu segments views into "My" (User-specific/Assigned) vs "Overall" (Company-wide/All) and lists: Dashboard, Profile, Listings (My/KD), Projects (Assigned/All), Enterprise Accounts (Assigned/All), High Ticket Leads (My City/Overall), Notifications, leads, Saved/Shortlisted. _(§ BR 2 Custom Side-Menu Segmentation)_
- **BR-KDT-020** — Dashboards must have a switch to toggle between "High-Value" and "Standard" inventory views. _(§ BR 2 Grid Toggles)_
- **BR-KDT-021** — Dashboard must offer filtering (e.g., City) and sorting (e.g., "Most Demands", "Most Properties Posted", "Most Leads Received"). _(§ BR 2 Filters & Sorting)_
- **BR-KDT-022** — Requirements exceeding per-city size thresholds (e.g., >10,000 sq ft Bangalore/Hyderabad; >5,000 sq ft Mumbai) are classified as HTLs. _(§ BR 3 HVL Definition)_
- **BR-KDT-023** — Admin panel must allow defining and editing HTL square-footage limits per city. _(§ BR 3 HVL Definition)_
- **BR-KDT-024** — HVLs are exclusively new, fresh inquiries or registrations that meet or exceed size thresholds based on asset class and city. _(§ BR 3 HVL Definition)_
- **BR-KDT-025** — HTL rules and threshold routing apply across Office, Retail and F&B asset classes. _(§ BR 3 Cross-Asset Application)_
- **BR-KDT-026** — Day-to-day operational requirements posted by existing, onboarded enterprise brands (e.g., Raymond, H&M) are not HVLs. _(§ BR 3 Exclusion)_
- **BR-KDT-027** — A new inquiry below the HV threshold bypasses RM notification and is instantly unlocked/visible to all existing agents (e.g., 6,000 sq ft restaurant vs 8,000 benchmark). _(§ BR 3 Standard Leads)_
- **BR-KDT-028** — HTL restrictions apply only to Tier 1 markets: Bangalore, Hyderabad, Chennai, Coimbatore, Pune, Mumbai, Gurgaon, Delhi. _(§ BR 3 Tier 1 vs Tier 2)_
- **BR-KDT-029** — Leads in Tier 2 cities (e.g., Jaipur, Indore) remain open to all agents regardless of size. _(§ BR 3 Tier 1 vs Tier 2)_
- **BR-KDT-030** — HTLs are routed exclusively to the Keydemand internal roster and are completely hidden from external agents. _(§ BR 3 Exclusive Routing)_
- **BR-KDT-031** — New-HTL notifications go only to the assigned city's KD members. _(§ BR 3 Global Access vs Local Alerts)_
- **BR-KDT-032** — All KD team members can view HTLs pan-India. _(§ BR 3 Global Access vs Local Alerts)_
- **BR-KDT-033** — If KD cannot service an HTL within a timeframe (e.g., 3-4 days), Admins can manually "unlock" it, pushing it into the public relevancy pool visible to external agents only via relevancy matching. _(§ BR 3 Manual Unlock Valve)_
- **BR-KDT-034** — Once an admin unlocks an HVL, notifications go only to agents with a relevant property matching the demand (standard demand workflow). _(§ BR 8 Notifications)_
- **BR-KDT-035** — Demands posted directly by agents bypass HTL restrictions and remain visible to other agents via relevancy matching. _(§ BR 3 Agent-Added Exemption)_

#### Open questions / ambiguities in this doc
- Hamburger 5 Leads: "By Status - Closed, New, Contacted - This is Phase 2. What is the plan" — explicit open question; Leads filters (New, Contacted, Qualified, Close) don't match the CRM stages (New, In Discussion, Site Visit, Negotiation, Closed, Lost) or the By Status list.
- Hamburger 1 dashboard numbers don't add up: Enterprise Users 500 → Assigned 50 → nested "All — 20" (Body 1.4 says All = 450); High Value leads is nested under Enterprise Users; Projects 250 = Assigned 50 + All 200, yet "All" means all projects on the platform.
- Body 1.5 defines "All" HVLs as "assigned to the rest of the team" (40), but the side menu says "High Ticket Leads (My City/Overall)", and BR 8 uses "Others"/"All" tabs. The labels are inconsistent.
- HVL threshold examples are inconsistent: >10,000 sq ft (Bangalore/Hyderabad), >5,000 sq ft (Mumbai), "5,000+ sq ft" (Body 1.5), benchmark 8,000 (restaurant example). The HTL city list leaves out Indore, which another Keydemand doc lists as an admin threshold city.
- Enterprise lead status: BR 5 says Approved/Rejected/Open; Body 1.4 flow and drill-downs say Approved/Rejected/Pending.
- "Phone number viewed" (Hamburger 1) = others viewing KD member's number (inbound), while the property-leads slider tab uses the same label for leads. Its direction is ambiguous.
- Body 1.6 "Property Agents" lists data columns (Subscription details, Properties added…) under "Filters". Is it filters or table columns? It also overlaps with "Broker Monitoring View" (BR 7) and the "Broker Management" permission.
- Exclusive projects (landing 4) says "Agents can show interest", but this is the KD page. It's unclear whether KD sees the Show Interest CTA on Exclusive projects (older docs said KD has no CTA on projects).
- Self Property/Demand Card CTA includes "Deactivate", but the Actions text says only "Edit and Delete".
- Header 2/3 text "add all other types of properties" for Post demand appears copy-pasted.
- BR 4 Image Request CTA rule names the CTA "View Image Request", but elsewhere it is "request for images".
- Enterprise Demand drill-down: "POC can edit/delete/deactive" conflicts with BR 5 Posting Restrictions (KD users assigned to a brand cannot post or edit demands on its behalf).
- Card field "Size of" (KD cards) appears incomplete.
- "Lead Statusing" sentence ends with a stray "6".

Account Demands, High Value Leads, Notifications & Enquiries, Saved / Shortlisted), footer ("Page 1 of 7"), 1 embedded comment, 3 image placements · read coverage: 100% (text via read_file_content; docx XML also downloaded and parsed for comments, tracked changes, header/footer, images; the only media file is a blank/decorative PNG)

#### Content
Document header: **KD — Hamburger Menu (V1 + V2)**

###### Business Rules
**1. Account Management & User Permissions**
- Onboarding & Authentication: Keydemand team members are onboarded exclusively via the backend and log in using their mobile number and an OTP.
- Role-Based Access: Account creation is strictly permission-based; specific privileges are managed via the admin portal.
- Profile Management Restrictions: The Keydemand team cannot edit, delete, or deactivate any user profiles via the front end; all profile management must be handled at the backend.
- Inventory Lifecycle: Deactivating a user profile automatically deactivates their associated inventory. Deleting a profile permanently removes all associated inventory.
- Team Inventory Capabilities: Keydemand members can view the inventory of other team members within their "Listings" dashboard, but they are strictly restricted to editing only their own self-listings.
- Backup Coordination: If multiple users are assigned to the same project, they function as backups and must coordinate their efforts offline.
- "My Listings" CRUD Privileges: Keydemand team must be granted full Create, Read, Update, and Delete (CRUD) privileges strictly over the properties and demands they have personally posted.
- "Keydemand Listings" (Colleague Data): Properties and Demands posted by other Key Demand team members must be strictly "Read-Only" for colleagues; users cannot edit, delete, or deactivate other colleague's listings.
- Future Phase (Scope): In a future release phase, Keydemand users will be permitted to add projects and developers directly.

**2. Login Flow & Dashboard Navigation**
- Immediate Dashboard Redirect: Keydemand users must be redirected straight to their Dashboard immediately upon logging in.
- Mobile UX Optimization: The mobile app interface must abandon horizontal tables in favour of a card/thumbnail-based layout to optimise screen space and usability.
- Dashboard Routing Logic:
  - Clicking on any user card must route the Keydemand user directly to a read-only view of that specific user's dashboard statistics.
- Interactive Drill-Downs: All aggregate metrics on the Dashboard (e.g., Active Properties, Active Demands, Projects) must be clickable, leading to a granular, filtered list view of the items being counted.
- Hamburger Menu & Holistic View: Keydemand Relationship Managers (RMs) must have a single holistic view from their user dashboard. By clicking the hamburger menu, they should see a summary of all assigned brands/tenants (demands, relevancies, contact requests, project inquiries) without needing to switch accounts.
- Custom Side-Menu Segmentation: A custom side-menu for keydemand users must bypass standard filters and segment views into "My" (User-specific/Assigned) vs. "Overall" (Company-wide/All). It must explicitly list: Dashboard, Profile, Listings (My/KD), Projects (Assigned/All), Enterprise Accounts (Assigned/All), High Ticket Leads (My City/Overall), Notifications, leads, and Saved/Shortlisted items.
- Grid Toggles: Dashboards must feature a dedicated switch to toggle between "High-Value" and "Standard" inventory views.
- Filters & Sorting: The dashboard must include comprehensive filtering (e.g., City) and sorting options (e.g., "Most Demands," "Most Properties Posted," "Most Leads Received").

**3. High-Ticket Lead (HTL) Ecosystem**
- HTL Definition & Dynamic Thresholds: Requirements exceeding specific size thresholds (e.g., >10,000 sq ft in Bangalore/Hyderabad; >5,000 sq ft in Mumbai) are classified as HTLs. The Admin must have controls in the panel to define and edit these square footage limits on a per-city basis.
- Cross-Asset Application: HTL rules and automated routing based on thresholds apply across Office, Retail, and F&B asset classes.
- Tier 1 vs. Tier 2 Routing: HTL restrictions only apply to Tier 1 markets (Bangalore, Hyderabad, Chennai, Coimbatore, Pune, Mumbai, Gurgaon, Delhi). Leads in Tier 2 cities (e.g., Jaipur, Indore) bypass this and remain open to all agents regardless of size.
- Exclusive Routing: HTLs are routed exclusively to the Keydemand internal roster and are completely hidden from external agents.
- Global Access vs. Local Alerts: While notifications for a new HTL are localized to the assigned city members, all Keydemand team members possess global access to view HTLs pan-India.
- Manual Unlock Valve: If the Keydemand team cannot service an HTL within a specific timeframe (e.g., 3-4 days), Admins can manually "unlock" the requirement. This pushes it into the public relevancy pool, making it visible to external agents strictly under the relevancy matching engine.
- Agent-Added Exemption: Demands posted directly by agents bypass HTL restrictions entirely and remain visible to other agents via relevancy matching.

**4. Visibility, Relevancy & Image Security**
- "Posted By" Transparency: To external audiences, internal demands/properties display as "Keydemand." However, internally, the team will see the specific name of the uploading team member (e.g., "Posted by Himanshu").
- Exclusive Indicators: If a demand is managed exclusively by Keydemand, the "Self-View" and explore demand screens must explicitly indicate "Keydemand Team".
- Hidden Image Protocols: If a listing owner selects "Do not show images", external users cannot view them. However, Keydemand teams can always see these images, overlaid with a banner reading "Hidden to others".
- Thumbnail Rule: The system must display property thumbnails to the Keydemand team in all list views, even if the primary images are hidden from public or external view.
- Image Request CTA Prevention: To prevent sourcing conflicts, the "View Image Request" CTA button must be completely removed (or greyed out/disabled) for Keydemand users when they view external agent properties.
- Relevancy Matching Scope: Matching for Keydemand is restricted solely to Brands and Tenants; the system does not match Keydemand against Agent properties or Agent demands (subject to final confirmation/TBD by Kartik).
- Demand Exploration Exclusivity: The Keydemand team is the only party authorised to explore demands. Specifically, "Managed Space" demands are visible exclusively to Keydemand and hidden from everyone else.

**5. Enterprise Accounts Breakdown & Pipeline Management**
- Enterprise Account Dashboard Breakdown: The dashboard must calculate the total aggregate of enterprise users (e.g., 500) and segment them into:
  - Assigned to Me: Total count assigned to the logged-in user.
  - Assigned to Others: Balance managed by the rest of the team.
  - Sub-Category Itemisation: The "Assigned to Me" count must explicitly break down into itemised values for Retail and Office Brands, Office Tenants, and Managed Spaces.
- Posting Restrictions: Keydemand users assigned to a brand cannot manually post or edit demands on that brand's behalf. Enterprise requirements must be managed via bulk or single upload centrally through the Admin panel.
- CRM Pipeline (Lite): The Admin Dashboard tracks enterprise leads through explicit CRM stages: New, In Discussion, Site Visit, Negotiation, Closed, Lost. It also logs the assigned representative and the last activity date. (Phase 2)
- Lead Statusing: Leads for Enterprise Clients are strictly categorised as Approved, Rejected, or Open.
- Alerting & Highlights: New relevancies, leads, and enquiries for assigned Enterprise clients must be visually highlighted with direct routing to the respective page.

**6. Action Tracking & Accountability Audits**
- Metric Definition ("User Contacted"): The "User Contacted" metric must increment exclusively when the "View Phone Number" button is clicked, as offline physical calls cannot be tracked.
- Direct Contact CTAs: The Keydemand team does not need to use "Request Phone Number" workflows for relevant demands; they are provided with an explicit "View Phone Number" CTA for direct, instant access.
- Outbound Contact Logs: "Properties Contacted" logs for Enterprise clients must capture the Property ID, associated photo, and the exact date of contact for audit purposes.
- Lead Access Audit Trail: Clicking the "View Requirement" CTA unlocks the lead's mobile number and automatically updates the "Viewed" status (Yes/No) with a timestamp.
- Accountability Tracking: A "Viewed by" column must maintain a timestamped log of exactly which Keydemand team member accessed a lead.

**7. Broker Management & Projects**
- Broker Monitoring View: A specialized, restricted dashboard view must exist for Business Development members to monitor the platform activity of external brokers they have onboarded. This tracks requirements added, relevancies, contact attempts, leads received, missed calls, and ignored image requests to counter broker complaints.
- Project Addition: Projects can only be added strictly via the backend control panel by the Admin team.
- Project Categorization: Projects must be sorted by "Category" (Standard, Premium, Exclusive) within the tables.
- Exclusive Project Follow-up: The Keydemand team is exclusively responsible for handling all follow-ups and contact for mandated "Exclusive" projects.
- Enquiry Granularity: All project lists must support a drill-down for "Enquiries Received," capturing user metadata (type, name, mobile, email, timestamp, and specific projects of interest).

**8. Notifications & Routing**
- Notification Filtering: Notifications must be segmentable, allowing users to filter by specific triggers such as "All leads for my listings," "Tagged projects," or "Relevancies".
- Enquiry Routing Logic: The system must automate routing based on the specific interaction type (e.g., direct developer enquiries, enterprise conversion prompts, or support requests)

### Group-level notes
#### Version history
- **Specific Page family.** Lineage: "Keydemand Team Specific Page - Registered" (created 2026-05-13, agent-template draft) → "Keydemand team- Specific Page" (created 2026-05-28, comment-driven rules June 12–29) → "Version 2 - Keydemand team- Specific Page" (2026-07-02, a clean copy of the former) → "Version 1.0 Keydemand Team Specific Page - Registered" (created 2026-08-10, restructured using the Dashboard docx business rules) → **"Version 2.0 Keydemand Team Specific Page - Registered"** (created 2026-09-28, modified 2026-10-06).
- "Version 2" and "Version 2.0" tie on version number, so the authority rule falls back to modified date: Version 2.0 (2026-10-06) beats Version 2 (2026-07-02). Content confirms it: "Version 2" belongs to the older lineage, and its title number is misleading.
- **Dashboard family.** "Version 1.0 - Keydemand Team- Dashboard 30062026 - Final.docx" is authoritative by its version number in the title. The unversioned "Keydemand Team- Dashboard 30062026 - Final.docx" is HISTORY, even though its modified date (2026-08-12) is later. Its text is the same apart from comments and one tracked change. The older doc 5 called the unversioned Dashboard docx "final".
- The two families overlap heavily. The Dashboard V1.0 business rules (sections 1–8) are an earlier copy of Specific Page V2.0 sections 1–7 and 9. Specific Page V2.0 is the later document (2026-10-06 vs 2026-08-10) and should prevail on overlapping rules.

#### Conflicts across docs in this group
- **Inventory on KD user deactivate/delete.** Specific Page V2.0 [AUTH]: listings must be reassigned to another KD user before delete/deactivate. Dashboard V1.0 [AUTH], Specific Page V1.0, doc 3 and doc 5: deactivate → inventory deactivated; delete → inventory permanently removed. Doc 4: delete is a soft delete retaining inventory; deactivate stops subscription. The latest rule is Specific Page V2.0.
- **KD relevancy matching scope.** Specific Page V2.0 [AUTH]: matched with own postings, other KD members, agents, brands and tenants. Dashboard V1.0 [AUTH] and Specific Page V1.0: restricted solely to Brands and Tenants, not Agent properties/demands ("subject to final confirmation/TBD by Kartik"). Docs 3/5: same restriction ("TBD - with Satish and Krishna"). The latest rule is Specific Page V2.0.
- **HVL labels and counts.** Dashboard V1.0: "High Value Ticket — 50: Assigned 10 / Others 40". Specific Page V2.0: "High Value leads — 50: Assigned 10 / All 40", with All defined as the rest of the team. Side menu: "High Ticket Leads (My City/Overall)". The Dashboard has an "All Leads" table with Assigned to / Viewed by; Specific Page V2.0 Body 1.5 only lists Assigned fields.
- **HVL threshold and city lists.** Examples vary: >10,000 (Bangalore/Hyderabad), >5,000 (Mumbai), 5,000+ (generic), 8,000 (restaurant), 15,000 (Mumbai example, doc 3/5). Tier 1 list (both AUTH docs): Bangalore, Hyderabad, Chennai, Coimbatore, Pune, Mumbai, Gurgaon, Delhi. Docs 3/5 admin threshold list includes Indore, which the AUTH docs class as Tier 2. Docs 3/5 exclude Managed offices from HVL; the AUTH docs say Office, Retail, F&B.
- **Enterprise lead statuses.** BR text: Approved/Rejected/Open. Drill-downs in both AUTH docs: Approved/Rejected/Pending. CRM-lite (Phase 2): New/In Discussion/Site Visit/Negotiation/Closed/Lost. Specific Page V2.0 Leads filters: New/Contacted/Qualified/Close.
- **Broker/agent monitoring.** Dashboard V1.0 has the "List of Brokers (External Agents)" table with Subscribed Yes/No/Expired. Specific Page V2.0 replaces it with "Property Agents" (Subscribed Yes/no, items listed as "Filters"). Both name the same drill-downs.
- **Menu structure.** Dashboard V1.0 menu: Dashboard, My Profile, Listings, Projects, Brands/Tenants, High Value Leads, Notifications, Enquiries, Shortlisted, List of Brokers, Sign out. Specific Page V2.0 hamburger: Dashboard, Edit profile, Saved, Notifications, Leads, Logout, with the other areas as Body dashboard tabs (Overview, Properties, Demands, Projects, Enterprise, High Value Leads, Property Agents).
- **Profile fields.** Dashboard V1.0: Name, Number, Email, Photo. Specific Page V2.0 adds Designation, Assigned city (Multiple) and a 13-item permission list.
- **Listing CTAs.** Dashboard V1.0 My listings Actions: Edit / Delete. Specific Page V2.0 Self cards: Edit, Deactivate, Delete.

Specific Page V2.0: Demand ID (POC can edit/delete/deactivate), Asset Class, Transaction, City, Location, Size, Relevancy, Leads. The POC edit right also conflicts with the Posting Restriction rule (both AUTH docs).
- **Project interest CTAs for KD.** Docs 3/5: KD needs no Show Interest CTA on Exclusive/Developer projects. Specific Page V2.0: Premium Projects "Keydemand team can show interest", and Exclusive projects / Projects in <city> keep Show Interest. Docs 1/2/4 Exclusive projects CTA: "Enquire Now" (V1.0) vs "Show Interest" (V2.0).

#### Content

##### Business Rules

**Platform Architecture & Environment Separation**
- **Strict Access Separation:** The platform must be strictly demarcated into two environments: the "Control Panel" (Admin portal) and the "User Portal".
- **Operational Demarcation:** 100% of day-to-day business operations (Sales, Business Development, Broker Management) must happen exclusively within the User Portal (Keydemand Team Dashboard), not the backend Control Panel.
- **Control Panel Access Limits:** The Control Panel is dedicated to the user management, bulk uploads, platform oversight, and configuring high-value leads, and must only be accessible to 4-5 core people (Kartik, Sudanshu, Himanshu, Nitesh, and tech admins).

**Admin Roles & Permissions**
- **Phase 1 Roles:** For the initial launch, enforce strictly three primary administrative roles in the Control Panel: "Super Admin", "Admin", and "Ops User".
- **Super Admin Privileges:** The Super Admin role must possess the highest system privileges, including the specific authority to delete or remove other Admins from the system.
- **Dynamic Role Creation:** The system must include functionality allowing the core admin team to create new internal user roles dynamically and toggle their access permissions across the platform.
- **Deferred Granular Permissions:** Highly granular, module-level permission toggles (e.g., manually unchecking specific view/edit/delete rights for internal admins) must be deferred to Phase 2 development to prevent over-engineering.
- Note: Check the possibilities of the dynamic access provision from the admin user while onboarding the other users(lower than his permissions level)
- **Admin Login Protocol:** Admin account creation requires a name, an email ID, and a set of permissions. Login operates via email and password, triggering a one-time password sent to the registered email upon creation, with options to change and reset passwords.
- **Complimentary Access for Testing:** Admins can assign zero-charge subscriptions to agents from the backend (e.g., to test agent journey access).

**Agent Onboarding & Front-End Privileges**
- **Mandatory Onboarding Fields:** Adding an agent requires: Name, Mobile Number, Email ID, Designation, Experience, WhatsApp On/Off, Profile Picture, Asset Class, Transaction Type, My City, and Company Name.
- **Default Front-End Permissions:** "Dashboard" access and "Explore Property" access must be set as default, non-removable permissions for all new Key Demand users.
- **Complimentary Access for Testing:** Admins can assign zero-charge subscriptions to agents from the backend (e.g., to test agent journey access).

**Keydemand Team Onboarding & Front-End Privileges**
- **No Self-Registration:** The Keydemand team is restricted from self-registering from the user portal; they must be added manually from the backend Control Panel by an Admin.
- **Mandatory Onboarding Fields:** When an Admin adds a Keydemand team, they must input their name, mobile number, email, designation, and specific city.
- **Default Front-End Permissions:** "Dashboard" access and "Explore Property" access must be set as default, non-removable permissions for all keydemand user roles.
- **Configurable Front-End Permissions:** Admins can selectively toggle a Keydemand team's ability to explore demands, post properties/demands, access broker management, view Keydemand listings, and view assigned enterprise brands.
- **Deactivation and Deletion of Keydemand team:** Yes, the listings needs to be assigned to another KD team user before they delete the account or deactivate

**Listing & Inventory Management**
- **"My Listings" CRUD Privileges:** Key Demand users must be granted full Create, Read, Update, and Delete (CRUD) privileges strictly over the properties and demands they have personally posted.
- **"Key Demand Listings" (Colleague Data):** Properties and demands posted by other Key Demand team members must be strictly "Read-Only" for colleagues; users cannot edit, delete, or deactivate another colleague's listings.
- **Control Panel Editing Limits:** Editing capabilities within the Listing Management Control Panel should only be enabled for "Keydemand" and "Enterprise" inventory.

**Enterprise Brand & Tenant Logic**
- **Enterprise Login:** Enterprise users (e.g., ABFRL) login using their registered mobile numbers.
- **Demand Auto-Fill Logic:** When an Enterprise user posts a demand and selects a Brand Name, the system must auto-fill all pre-configured brand information maintained in the backend format based on the brand format selection. The user only needs to complete the remaining mandatory or specific fields and should be able to edit the pre-populated field values.
- **Brand Image Display Logic:** If a brand logo/image is uploaded in the backend, it must display as the demand image. If no brand image is available, the system must default to displaying the selected "end-use" image.
- **Brand Deactivation Rule:** Admins can deactivate a brand under an Enterprise account. Upon deactivation, the brand immediately loses login access, and all its active demands must be disabled immediately.
- **Brand Reactivation Rule:** If an Admin reactivates a previously disabled brand, the system must only reinstate the brand account, not its previously active demands.
- **Brand & Tenant Contact View Limit:** Individual brands and tenants can view a maximum of 5 contact phone numbers across listings. Upon reaching this limit, the platform must display a prompt encouraging them to upgrade to Enterprise Solutions for unlimited access.

**Developer & Managed Space Operator Backend Setup**
- **Developer Onboarding Fields:** To add a Developer from the Control Panel, the Admin must input: Developer Name, Upload Logo, Mobile Number, Contact Name, Cities (multi-select), and Asset Class (multi-select).
- **Operator Onboarding Fields:** To add a Managed Space Operator, the Admin inputs: Operator Name, Mobile Number, Contact Name, and Cities (multi-select). The Asset Class is pre-selected by default to Managed Office Space.
- **Project Categorisation:** Added projects must be manually assigned to a category: Exclusive, Premium, or Common Project.

**High-Value Leads (HVL) & Relevancy Rules**
- **Demand Size Limit Logic:** The system must hide high-sq-ft demands (e.g., >10,000 sq ft) from standard users/agents and route them directly to the Keydemand team. HVL is only for demands
- **Size Configuration Feature:** The Admin portal must include a feature to dynamically control and configure these size limits per specific metro city. Not just size but also the city, asset class and size as written in the document below.
- **HVL Unopened Marker:** Unopened leads must be visually marked with a red dot in the platform.
- **HVL Unlock Notification:** If the Keydemand team unlocks an HVL requirement, the system must notify normal agents too besides to key demand agents who possess relevant properties based on relevancy matching.
- **HVL Notification Mediums:** Notifications for new leads must go out via both email and WhatsApp to the assigned users.
- **HVL Customisation:** The HVL section must be highly customizable, allowing edits for each city, asset class, size range, and assigned Keydemand team members from the Admin Panel.
- **Visibility Rules:**
  - All KD team members must be able to access/view all high-value leads.
  - Demands added by agents must be visible to other agents (under relevancy), regardless of size constraints.
  - Leads from other cities can be viewed by agents and the entire Keydemand team (under relevancy), irrespective of size.

**Subscription, Pricing & City Management**
- **Immediate Frontend Pricing Updates:** Price changes made by Admins via the Control Panel must reflect on the front end immediately.
- **Deferred Billing Cycle Impact:** For active users, updated subscription prices will only take effect and bill starting from their next billing cycle.
- **No City Deletion (Phase 1):** The ability to "Delete" a city from the system is strictly disabled for Phase 1 to prevent catastrophic system conflicts for external agents(WebApp users) with active auto-pay/auto-renewal tokens.
- **Tier Management:** Admins can edit subscription prices and add new cities to specific categorisations (Class A/Metros, Class B/Non-metros, Class C/Rest of India, Class D/Pan India).
- **Indicative Cities Protection:** Existing indicative cities pre-populated within the tiers must not be removed from their respective categories.

**Card Identification, User Tags & Layout Controls**
- **Card Identification & User Tags:** All property and project cards must display clear identification tags distinguishing whether a listing was posted by an Agent or a Direct Owner.
- **CTA Repositioning on Cards:** Calls to Action (CTAs) on detailed cards must be prominently positioned in both the top and bottom folds to ensure seamless user engagement without excessive scrolling.
- **Audit Trail & Viewed-By Logs:** The backend must maintain a timestamped audit trail recording every instance a Keydemand team member accesses or views high-value leads or specific client requirements.

**V1 to V2 Platform Transition Actions**
- **Automated Migration:** All active V1 users must be automatically migrated to the new V2 platform.
- **Complimentary Transition Access:** At the time of go-live, the Admin team must manually use the Control Panel to assign 3 months of complimentary Pan-India access to all migrated V1 users.

**Data Management, Exports, & Analytics**
- **CSV Exports:** The Control Panel must support two master CSV downloads:
  - **User Management CSV:** Downloads the complete directory of users across the platform.
  - **Listing Level CSV:** Downloads all properties, demands, and projects.
- **Analytics Sync:** Google Analytics tracking (Daily, Weekly, and Monthly data points) will be embedded into the User Dashboards. Full synchronization within the Admin Control Panel is deferred to Phase 2 development.

When a user uploads a demand under an Enterprise account (e.g., ABFRL), they can log in using their registered mobile number.

While posting a demand:
- The user first selects the Brand Name (e.g., Arrow) or Allen Solly etc.
- Once the brand is selected, all pre-configured brand information maintained in the backend under(Format) will be auto-filled.
- The user only needs to complete the remaining mandatory fields and any additional information specific to that requirement.

Brand Image Logic:
- If a brand logo/image has been uploaded in the backend, it should be displayed as the demand image.
- If no brand image is available, the selected end-use image should be displayed instead.
- End use images are in this drive link: <https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1tLzp1TPq7mAbEqZMl-4g_OLCEHYI_08W>

Brand Deactivation:
- The admin should have the option to deactivate a brand under an Enterprise account.
- Once deactivated, the brand will no longer be able to log in, and all its active demands should be disabled immediately. It should also have an option to activate as well which will re-instate the brand only and not the demands.

**Templates & Samples.** The Templates & Samples tab on the [Bulk Upload](https://admin-uat-v2.keydemand.in/listings/bulk-upload) page organizes downloadable templates into three main sections. Each one has options to view samples, download spreadsheets (.xlsx or .csv), preview fields, or start an upload:
- **Demands**: Space requirements posted by brands, tenants, agents, or the Keydemand team.
  - Demand · Retail · Lease (brand) (3 sample rows)
  - Demand · Retail · Buy (brand) (2 sample rows)
  - Demand · F&B · Lease (brand) (2 sample rows)
  - Demand · Office · Lease (tenant) (1 sample row)
  - Demand · Office · Buy (tenant) (1 sample row)
  - Demand · Managed Space · Lease (1 sample row)
  - Demand · Retail · Lease (agent) (1 sample row)
  - Demand · Enterprise Format mode (3 sample rows — Format: only City and Location change per row)
- **Properties**: Retail, F&B, and office listings posted by agents or the Keydemand team.
  - Property · Retail · Lease (2 sample rows)
  - Property · Retail · Sale (1 sample row)
  - Property · F&B · Lease (2 sample rows)
  - Property · F&B · Sale (1 sample row)
  - Property · Office · Lease (1 sample row)
  - Property · Office · Sale (1 sample row)
- **Projects & Centres**: Developer projects and managed-space centres posted for an operator.
  - Project · Developer · Office (1 sample row)
  - Project · Developer · Retail / Mixed use (1 sample row)
  - Centre · Managed office (1 sample row)
  - Centre · Flex (multiple formats) (1 sample row)
- For each entry listed above, you can access actions such as [Sample], [Template .xlsx], [.csv], [Preview fields], and [Start upload].
- Validation document for bulk upload summary and forms: <https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1sDfBmuKUh_Q21_SSudXkGKDHdalGwklK4iPAyQLEfNk/edit?gid=1215127467#gid=1215127467>

**When clicked on Upload properties: New Bulk Upload.** Steps Bar: 1 Configure, 2 Upload, 3 Validate, 4 Preview, 5 Create for review, 6 Review & approve

1. **Configure** ("What are you uploading?")
   - Create: Demand, Property, Project, Centre
   - Asset class: Retail, F&B, Office, Managed Space
   - Transaction: Lease, Buy
   - Post as: Brand, Agent, Keydemand Team
   - Search Brand: Search bar (with a list of brand profiles such as "K4 Brand outsider", "K4 Brand holder", "QA352 Brand", etc.)
   - Actions: Blank template: Download .xlsx, Download .csv, Preview fields; Continue (Button)
   - Information Panel: **What will happen**: Details about approval workflows, 60-day expiry rules, and routing rules for High Value Leads across cities (Mumbai, Pune, Delhi, Hyderabad, Bengaluru). **Need a sample?**: Downloadable sample templates (Sample, Template .xlsx, .csv, Preview fields) for: Demand · Retail · Lease (brand); Demand · Retail · Lease (agent); Demand · Enterprise Format mode
   - Once we select the continue button after selecting the brand →
2. **Upload**
   - Header: Upload your file
   - Configuration Summary: Demand · Retail · Lease · Brand · posted as K4 Brand
   - File Dropzone: "Drag & drop your .xlsx or .csv here"; "or browse" (Link to open file explorer)
   - File constraints: up to 5 MB · 2,000 rows
   - Action Buttons: [← Back] (Returns to the Configure step); [↑ Upload & validate] (Currently inactive; activates once a file is selected)
3. **Validate**
   - Alert/Status Box: "No issues — every row passed."
   - Filters & Toggles: Tabs: All (2), Valid (2), Warnings (0), Errors (0), Duplicates (0); Toggle: HVL only
   - Data Table columns: ROW, STATUS, SUMMARY, ISSUES; Row Data; Pagination
   - Action Buttons (Bottom): Download error file; Re-upload fixed file; Revalidate; Cancel job; Create demands for review → (CTA Primary Action)
4. **Preview**
   - Modal Fields & Toggles: Include rows with warnings; Include duplicates
   - Action Buttons: Cancel; Create
5. **Create for review**
   - Tabs / Filters: Pending review; Blocked; Approved; Rejected
   - Action Buttons: Select all on this page; Reject selected; Approve selected; Approve all eligible
   - Table Columns: Checkbox (Select); ID; Listing; Posted As; Flags; Issues; State
6. **Review & approve**: Once we approve, it goes live. We can edit it too later on.

Templates & Samples: Are all listed here. <https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1vE8L1BGFQOthubB4WFlAoFe5faDaUVOBCSZfPwzqq08/edit?gid=0#gid=0>

#### Business rules extracted
- **BR-ADM-001** — The platform must be strictly demarcated into two environments: the "Control Panel" (Admin portal) and the "User Portal". _(§ Business Rules › Platform Architecture)_
- **BR-ADM-002** — 100% of day-to-day business operations (Sales, Business Development, Broker Management) must happen exclusively within the User Portal (Keydemand Team Dashboard), not the backend Control Panel. _(§ Platform Architecture)_
- **BR-ADM-003** — The Control Panel is dedicated to user management, bulk uploads, platform oversight, and configuring high-value leads, and must only be accessible to 4-5 core people (Kartik, Sudanshu, Himanshu, Nitesh, and tech admins). _(§ Platform Architecture)_
- **BR-ADM-004** — Phase 1 enforces strictly three primary administrative roles in the Control Panel: "Super Admin", "Admin", and "Ops User". _(§ Admin Roles & Permissions)_ — conflicts with doc 3 and doc 4 (two roles)
- **BR-ADM-005** — The Super Admin role possesses the highest system privileges, including the authority to delete or remove other Admins. _(§ Admin Roles & Permissions)_
- **BR-ADM-006** — The system must allow the core admin team to create new internal user roles dynamically and toggle their access permissions across the platform. _(§ Admin Roles & Permissions)_
- **BR-ADM-007** — Highly granular, module-level permission toggles (e.g., unchecking specific view/edit/delete rights for internal admins) are deferred to Phase 2. _(§ Admin Roles & Permissions)_ — conflicts with the Add Control Panel User modal, which lists granular toggles (BR-ADM-075)
- **BR-ADM-008** — Admin account creation requires a name, an email ID, and a set of permissions. _(§ Admin Login Protocol)_
- **BR-ADM-009** — Admin login is via email and password. On creation, a one-time/temporary password is emailed to the registered email, and the user resets it on first login. Change-password and reset-password options exist. _(§ Admin Login Protocol; § Control Panel Users)_
- **BR-ADM-010** — Admins can assign zero-charge (complimentary) subscriptions to agents from the backend (e.g., to test agent journey access). _(§ Admin Roles; § Agent Onboarding)_
- **BR-ADM-011** — Adding an agent requires: Name, Mobile Number, Email ID, Designation, Experience, WhatsApp On/Off, Profile Picture, Asset Class, Transaction Type, My City, and Company Name. _(§ Agent Onboarding)_

- **BR-ADM-013** — The Keydemand team cannot self-register from the user portal. They must be added manually from the backend Control Panel by an Admin. _(§ Keydemand Team Onboarding)_
- **BR-ADM-014** — Adding a Keydemand team member requires name, mobile number, email, designation and specific city. The Add form also captures Profile Picture and Assigned city (Multiple). _(§ Keydemand Team Onboarding; § 1.1 Keydemand Team)_

- **BR-ADM-016** — Before a Keydemand team member's account is deleted or deactivated, their listings must be assigned to another KD team user. _(§ Keydemand Team Onboarding)_
- **BR-ADM-017** — "Pending handovers" holds the work of departed KD members. An admin hands each item to an active member, and the member's accounts, listings, assignments and pending enquiries move together. _(§ 1.1 Keydemand Team)_
- **BR-ADM-018** — Key Demand users have full CRUD strictly over the properties and demands they personally posted ("My Listings"). _(§ Listing & Inventory)_
- **BR-ADM-019** — Listings posted by other KD team members are strictly Read-Only for colleagues. Users cannot edit, delete or deactivate a colleague's listings. _(§ Listing & Inventory)_
- **BR-ADM-020** — In Control Panel Listing Management, editing is enabled only for "Keydemand" and "Enterprise" inventory. _(§ Listing & Inventory)_
- **BR-ADM-021** — Enterprise users (e.g., ABFRL) log in using their registered mobile numbers. _(§ Enterprise Brand & Tenant Logic)_

The user completes the remaining mandatory/specific fields and can edit the pre-populated values. _(§ Enterprise Brand & Tenant Logic)_

#### Open questions / ambiguities in this doc
- **"Ops User"** role is named as a third Phase 1 role, but no permissions or capabilities are defined anywhere.
- Business rules defer "granular, module-level permission toggles" to Phase 2, yet the Add Control Panel User modal and the UAT page (doc 4) already show per-action toggles (27 permissions).
- "Note: Check the possibilities of the dynamic access provision from the admin user while onboarding the other users(lower than his permissions level)" is unresolved.
- Default permission "for all new Key Demand users" appears under *Agent* Onboarding. It is unclear whether this means agents or the KD team.
- HVL threshold example ">10,000 sq ft" vs per-city configuration. No defaults listed (doc 2 says Mumbai >5,000; Bangalore/Hyderabad >10,000).
- Project category naming is inconsistent: "Exclusive, Premium, Common Project" (rules); "Featured, Exclusive, Sponsored" (Booster); doc 2 uses "Standard/Premium/Exclusive".
- The Developer/MSO forms in the UI list extra fields (Email, Company, Designation, GST) that the Business Rules don't list. The MSO form lists "Company" twice.
- The Rest of India price is "₹1,000 flat" in the pricing table but "1000 INR checkbox" on the grant form. Retail & F&B grant form omits Rest of India / PAN India options (only Office lists them). Possibly an omission.
- The Enterprise "Arrow" profile is tagged "F&B | Individual" yet shows "Convert to Individual". The Office Enterprise "Zoho" is tagged "Individual" with "Convert to Individual". Looks like copy errors.
- "PROJECT ID | PROJECT ID" duplicated column headers in multiple relevancy tables (vs "PROJECT NAME | PROJECT ID" elsewhere).
- The Office & Managed Space tenants (Enterprise) table has a "LEFT" column with no definition.
- HVL "Add Rule" block appears both inside the KD-member Enterprise section and under 1.5 HVL › Cities. The placement looks accidental.
- Control Panel Users: "He will then login … and then set a username and password", but login is by email ID. It is unclear whether a username exists.
- The "Select City" field on the Control Panel user form has no stated purpose.
- The source says "Site Down" is Phase 2, while doc 4 lists "Site Down: Toggle" as a live permission.
- The Managed Space project table (present in doc 3) is missing from V2.0 Listing Management › Projects. Only the Developer table is given.

### Super Admin, Normal Admin what they can do  [AUTHORITATIVE]
**Source:** gdoc · ID `1qh1Uh-T8MWhGs2WumwpJY8mzXv3v9UhEVE2N4vp2cak` · pradeepa.pv@futuristglobal.com · modified 2026-08-27 · sections read: role table, Role Details & Context, Fields on the UAT Page, What a Super Admin Can Do, Manage User Modal, What a Regular / Standard Admin Can Do, comparison table · read coverage: 100% (no comments present)

#### Content

| Role | Primary Capabilities |
|---|---|
| **Super Admin** | Possesses the highest system privileges, including the authority to delete or remove other Admins from the system and full access to all modules. [1] |
| **Admin** | Manages day-to-day backend operations, including user management (adding/deleting/editing agents, tenants, developers, operators), listing management, subscription/city management, and handling High-Value Leads (HVL). [1] |
| **Normal User (Agent/Tenant/Enterprise)** | Operates within the "User Portal" (not the Control Panel). Capabilities include managing their own listings ("My Listings"), exploring properties/demands, and viewing relevant leads, depending on permissions configured by Admins. [1] |

[1] = citation link to https://docs.google.com/document/d/1TzelTFc-ie1E1pp1zFwMXDEAI8RGhvEA/edit (the Version 1.0 Control Panel doc)

**Role Details & Context**
- **Administrative Access:** The Control Panel is restricted to 4-5 core people (Kartik, Sudanshu, Himanshu, Nitesh, and tech admins). Phase 1 enforces strictly two primary roles: "Super Admin" and "Admin". [1]
- **Normal User Constraints:**
  - **Keydemand Team:** Restricted from self-registering; must be added manually by an Admin. They have default "Dashboard" and "Explore Property" permissions. [1]
  - **Agent/Tenant Permissions:** Admins can selectively toggle an agent's ability to explore demands, post properties/demands, and access broker management. [1]
  - **Listing Visibility:** Key Demand users have CRUD privileges for their own listings. Other colleagues' listings are "Read-Only". [1]

**Fields on the UAT Page**
- **User Management Modal Fields**
- **Account Details**: Name (text input), Email ID (fixed/read-only), and City (text input).
- **Permission Controls**: Toggleable permissions across 11 modules:
  - *Dashboard*: View
  - *User Management*: View, Add, Edit, Delete, Enable / disable
  - *Listing Management*: View, Edit, Delete, Enable / disable
  - *Projects*: View, Add, Edit, Delete
  - *Subscription Management*: Manage cities, Edit pricing
  - *High Value Leads*: Manage rules, Toggle cities, Unlock leads, View leads
  - *Formats*: Manage
  - *Enquiries*: View, Manage
  - *Control Panel Users*: Manage
  - *Analytics*: View
  - *Content*: Manage
  - *Site Down*: Toggle

**What a Super Admin Can Do**
A Super Admin holds unrestricted backend access with all **27 out of 27 permissions** enabled across the platform:
- **User & Role Administration**: Create, edit, deactivate, or remove backend control panel users, and manage account access across 22 roles including Agents, Retail Brands, Managed Tenants, Developers, and Keydemand Team members.
- **Property & Listing Operations**: Add, update, view, or delete property listings and development projects.
- **Lead & Subscription Control**: Edit pricing structures, manage supported cities, set rules for High Value Leads (HVL), view lead data, and unlock premium leads.
- **System & Content Management**: Handle incoming customer enquiries, review platform analytics, edit site content, and toggle emergency system settings like "Site Down" mode.

**Manage User Modal**
- **Account Section**:
  - *Name*: Editable text field for the user's name.
  - *Email ID*: Read-only text field (cannot be edited after account creation).
  - *City*: Editable text field for location.
- **Permissions Section**: Selectable permission toggles broken down across 11 modules: (same list as above: Dashboard: View; User Management: View, Add, Edit, Delete, Enable / disable; Listing Management: View, Edit, Delete, Enable / disable; Projects: View, Add, Edit, Delete; Subscription Management: Manage cities, Edit pricing; High Value Leads: Manage rules, Toggle cities, Unlock leads, View leads; Formats: Manage; Enquiries: View, Manage; Control Panel Users: Manage; Analytics: View; Content: Manage; Site Down: Toggle)

**What a Regular / Standard Admin Can Do**
A standard admin user operates with granular, role-based access rather than full platform control:
- **Role-Restricted Workflows**: They can only view or interact with the specific modules enabled for them out of the 27 total permissions (for example, the user selected in the screenshot only has 3 permissions: viewing the Dashboard and viewing/adding Users). [Image: screenshot of a user with 3 permissions, not visible]
- **Specific Operational Tasks**: Depending on their granted permissions, they can be restricted to limited tasks like creating listings, handling customer enquiries, or viewing analytics without modifying global settings.
- **Limited Administrative Access**: Standard users generally cannot manage other internal control panel users, change subscription pricing, edit site content, or toggle critical controls like "Site Down" unless explicitly granted those individual permissions by a Super Admin.

| Feature / Capability | Super Admin | Standard Admin (Regular Admin) | Normal User (Agent / Tenant / Enterprise / Keydemand Team) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **System Access & Portal** | Unrestricted, full access to the Control Panel. | Granular, role-restricted backend access to the Control Panel. | Restricted entirely to the **"User Portal"** (cannot access the Control Panel). |
| **Permissions Configuration** | Holds all **27 out of 27 permissions** enabled across the platform. | Role-based; operates with restricted permissions, only interacting with modules enabled for them. | Access is determined and toggled by Admins (e.g., permission to explore demands, post properties, or access broker management). |
| **User & Role Administration** | **Create, edit, deactivate, or remove** backend control panel users (including deleting other Admins) and manage access across 22 roles. | **Limited user management** (adding/deleting/editing agents, tenants, developers, operators) but cannot manage other internal control panel users. | **No administrative privileges**. Keydemand Team members cannot self-register and must be added manually by an Admin. |
| **Property & Listing Operations** | Full authority to add, update, view, or delete any property listings and development projects. | Manage listings (view, edit, delete, enable/disable) depending on the specific modules enabled for their account. | Keydemand users have **CRUD privileges only for their own listings** ("My Listings"), while other colleagues' listings are strictly **"Read-Only"**. |
| **Lead & Subscription Control** | Edit pricing structures, manage supported cities, set rules for High Value Leads (HVL), and unlock premium leads. | Access to subscription/city management and HVL handling is restricted unless explicitly granted by a Super Admin. | Explore properties/demands and view relevant leads based on the permissions configured by the Admins. |
| **System & Content Management** | Handle enquiries, review analytics, edit site content, and toggle emergency controls like **"Site Down"** mode. | Cannot change pricing, edit site content, or toggle **"Site Down"** unless explicitly granted permissions. | No system or content management capabilities. |

#### Business rules extracted
- **BR-ADM-082** — Super Admin has the highest privileges, including authority to delete/remove other Admins, and full access to all modules. _(§ role table)_
- **BR-ADM-083** — Super Admin holds all 27 of 27 permissions. _(§ What a Super Admin Can Do)_
- **BR-ADM-084** — Super Admin can create, edit, deactivate or remove backend control panel users and manage account access across 22 roles. _(§ What a Super Admin Can Do)_
- **BR-ADM-085** — Admin manages day-to-day backend operations: user management (add/delete/edit agents, tenants, developers, operators), listing management, subscription/city management and HVL handling. _(§ role table)_
- **BR-ADM-086** — A Standard Admin can only view or interact with the modules enabled for them out of the 27 permissions. _(§ Regular / Standard Admin)_
- **BR-ADM-087** — A Standard Admin cannot manage other internal control panel users, change subscription pricing, edit site content or toggle "Site Down" unless explicitly granted those permissions by a Super Admin. _(§ Regular / Standard Admin; comparison table)_
- **BR-ADM-088** — Phase 1 enforces strictly two primary roles: "Super Admin" and "Admin". _(§ Role Details & Context)_ — conflicts with BR-ADM-004
- **BR-ADM-089** — Normal Users (Agent/Tenant/Enterprise/KD Team) operate only in the User Portal and cannot access the Control Panel. _(§ comparison table)_
- **BR-ADM-090** — Admins can selectively toggle an agent's ability to explore demands, post properties/demands and access broker management. _(§ Role Details & Context)_ — conflicts with doc 6 / doc 2, where demand exploration is KD-team-exclusive
- **BR-ADM-091** — In the Manage User modal, Email ID is read-only (cannot be edited after account creation). Name and City are editable. _(§ Manage User Modal)_
- **BR-ADM-092** — The Control Panel user permission set is 11–12 modules: Dashboard(View); User Mgmt(View, Add, Edit, Delete, Enable/disable); Listing Mgmt(View, Edit, Delete, Enable/disable); Projects(View, Add, Edit, Delete); Subscription(Manage cities, Edit pricing); HVL(Manage rules, Toggle cities, Unlock leads, View leads); Formats(Manage); Enquiries(View, Manage); Control Panel Users(Manage); Analytics(View); Content(Manage); Site Down(Toggle). These total 27 toggles. _(§ Fields on the UAT Page)_

#### Open questions / ambiguities in this doc
- It says "11 modules" but lists 12 (Dashboard, User Mgmt, Listing Mgmt, Projects, Subscription, HVL, Formats, Enquiries, Control Panel Users, Analytics, Content, Site Down). The 12 sum to 27 toggles (1+5+4+4+2+4+1+2+1+1+1+1). V2.0 adds "Bulk Upload" (2 toggles) and drops "Site Down", which also gives 27.
- "22 roles" is not enumerated anywhere.
- Citations point to the Version 1.0 Control Panel doc (`1TzelTFc…`), but the current text of that docx does not contain these statements. They appear in V2.0 and Keydemand.docx instead.
- The "Admin" row says Admin can add/delete users, but the Standard Admin text says those abilities depend on granted permissions. It is unclear whether "Admin" is a fixed role or a permission set.
